text:
St. Louis is 8-8-2, and our numbers say that's exactly what it has earned: about 18.6 points deserved, 18 banked. The Blues get 49% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), and the playoff odds are 28% in our simulations with a projection near 87 points. This is a bubble team waiting for something to tip it.

The top line is the reason for hope. Robert Thomas, Dylan Holloway and Jimmy Snuggerud were reunited after a push to put them back together, and they get 54% of the chances. Snuggerud has been scoring on the power play, Thomas added a shorthanded goal, and the newer group of Mason McTavish, Connor McMichael and Jonatan Berggren is generating chances too.

The warning sign is the power play as a whole. It creates about half a goal of expected offense per game, tied for the lowest of any team in this group, which is a lot of wasted opportunity for a club that needs every edge. And Justin Barron's hot run, 9 points in 10 games against 3.9 expected, is the kind that ends.

Joel Hofer has been left exposed on some nights, and Blues goalies are allowing about four more goals than expected. Colton Parayko's return should help. A win over Detroit on Tuesday kept them level. What to watch: whether the power play finds a second unit that can score, because five on five alone isn't going to lift this team out of the middle.
headline: The Blues are a .500 team, honestly
